units.text: Since sixteen you have put work, study and friends before money, and your income has followed your decades more than any plan of your own.
From your mid-thirties you shape your money around a partner, the home and a life of your own, and each decade sets how far it stretches.
From your late forties, you measure money by what it lets you give the people after you, with each decade setting how much comes in.
From sixteen you carry the family ways your first home taught you, while each decade sets the tone between you and your parents and siblings.
From your mid-thirties you shape family life around a partner and the home you keep, carrying the ways your earlier gates set as each decade turns.
From your late forties, you meet your family through the people after you, with each decade deciding who gathers close.
From sixteen you run your body on the reserve your childhood gave you, as work and study come first and each decade sets your strength.
From your mid-thirties you stay well on habits formed long before, drawing on the strength each decade brings to your home and your days.
From your late forties, you take your energy from the decade you are in, and the people after you give your days their shape.
From sixteen you take work as it comes through study, friends and family, and each decade turns the jobs of the moment into a direction.
From your mid-thirties you fit work around the home and the life you have chosen, while each decade decides how far your career climbs.
From your late forties, you put your work into the people after you and the hours that are yours, and each decade sets what it asks of you.
Since sixteen you have kept friends around the edges of a full week of study, work and family, with each decade deciding who stays close.
From your mid-thirties you meet your circle by plan more than by chance, as home and a partner fill your evenings and each decade brings its own faces.
From your late forties, you keep company with the people after you and the friends who have lasted, with each new decade adding faces to the circle.
Since sixteen you have learned by doing more than by study, with each decade choosing the questions your work and friendships bring you.
From your mid-thirties you put your mind to the work and the home in front of you, and each decade sets the subjects that hold you.
From your late forties, you turn your curiosity to practical things and to the people after you, while each decade sets what holds your attention.
Since sixteen you have grown through work, friends and family more than through any plan to improve yourself, as each decade brings its own change.
From your mid-thirties you grow through the life you already have, the work and the home, while each decade sets the pace of change.
From your late forties, you grow by settling into who you are and by teaching what you know to the people after you, as each decade turns.
Each decade moves your health more than any single habit of yours. You feel well for some stretches of years and worn for others, with each turn arriving as one decade gives way to the next.
Your money answers to each decade, and you trust one good year less than most people do. You read the turn before anyone around you does, because some decades bring it in and others draw it out.
Your thinking takes its colour from each decade, studious in one and restless or practical in another. You notice the change in what you read before you notice it in yourself.
Your growth moves at the speed of the decade you are in. You change fast in some decades and stand still in others, and only once one ends do you see which kind it was.
Your friendships follow no fixed pattern of their own. You have crowded years and quiet ones, and the change arrives with the decade more than with any choice you make.
Your money rises and falls with each decade.
Your health moves with the decade you are in.
Your thinking changes character with each decade.
Your growth keeps the pace of each decade.
Your circle widens and thins with the decades.
The character that rules your money arrives later in your life. Until then you earn and spend by the decade you are in, each one setting its own course.
Your money finds its own character later in life.
Your health has a character of its own that arrives in a later chapter, and for now each decade steers it. You take your strength from the years you are in, reading your energy one season at a time.
Your health answers to each decade for now.

Your career waits on a character who arrives later in life, and until then each decade sets its course. You take the work in front of you as it comes, building a direction one stretch of years at a time.
Your career takes its course from the decades for now.

The character that shapes your family arrives in a later chapter, and for now each decade sets how you belong. You show up for your family in the ways each stretch of years allows, closer in some and freer in others.
Your family life waits on a later chapter.
Your friendships get their own character later in life, and for now each decade sets the course. You make friends by the decade, adding to your circle as each one turns.
Your friendships find their own character in time.
Your mind has its own character still to come, and for now each decade sets what you think about. You follow the questions your present years raise, one subject at a time.
Your mind follows each decade until its own character arrives.
Your growth meets its own character later, and for now each decade sets the pace. You grow in step with the years you are in, changing when they ask it of you.
Your growth keeps time with the decades for now.
You lose money most easily where you share it with friends and family, and you also find your safety net among those same people.
With your people and your money at one gate, you rarely own anything that is only yours.
Underneath, you turn each result into standing, though you rarely ask for the title it has already earned you.
You also turn money into position, feeling richer when a gain comes with respect than when it comes alone.
You keep money and rank at one gate, where each gain argues quietly for your next step up.
You also find your mentors inside the structures you join, where your name gathers weight the slow and lasting way.
You also learn well inside a frame like a school or a discipline, studying on long after the course has ended.
You carry rank and learning at one gate, and neither grows in you without the other.
Underneath, you come out of every hard stretch at work more senior than you went in, and the pattern grows stronger with age.
Underneath, you answer the years that weigh on you with study and the people who steady you, ending every heavy stretch more sure of who you are.
Underneath, you turn pressure into understanding, and the hardest years of your life are the ones that taught you how to think.
In you the two sit at one gate, and you rarely meet a pressure without learning from it.
You also keep correcting the very structures you climb, doing your brightest work wherever the rules are loosest.
Your voice and your role share one gate, which leaves you arguing first with the position you hold.
Your boldest ideas and your patience for study also feed each other, with every qualification you earn making you braver in public.
You also learn best when you can show what you learn, turning every course you finish into something you can say out loud.
Your talent and your training sit at one gate, close enough that you rarely have to choose between them.
What you make turns into money more easily for you than for most, and the work that feels like play is the work that pays you best.
You also rise by making more rather than by climbing, as each piece of work you finish brings the next one to your door.
Because making and earning share a gate, you barely see a line between your craft and your income.
Underneath, you do your calmest work closest to pressure, because the deadlines that grind other people turn into steady output in your hands.
You find your protection in comfort, because good food and work with your hands turn pressure into something you can use.
With ease and pressure at one gate, you keep a firm hold on every strain that reaches you.
You also think so long about a thing that you miss the moment to make it, keeping a drawer of nearly finished work.
You also polish your work in private until the moment to show it has passed, and you lose more chances by not finishing than by failing.
You also forget to eat and sleep properly in your heaviest thinking seasons, with your body telling you before your mind admits it.
You hold thinking and making at one gate, and the thinking wins most of their arguments.
